page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-3840s-amd is an x86_64 architecture server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, consisting of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2912.97. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the middle 50% average range, scoring 46204.81 in stress-ng and 31969.29 in Passmark. Memory bandwidth tests show average tier performance, with uncached large-block reads at 123.94 GB/sec and writes at 70.41 GB/sec. Database and web serving operations also align with average tier expectations, yielding 28.04 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 15.37 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The server offers a high ratio of memory and NVMe storage relative to its vCPU count, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring substantial local storage and memory capacity without needing top-tier multi-core compute scaling. However, the 2.0 GHz base clock speed and average multi-core scaling represent a tradeoff for compute-bound tasks. This configuration is suitable for database hosting, memory-intensive applications, static web serving, and moderate-scale text processing or LLM inference workloads.
